subject: science
domain: From Molecules to Organisms: Structures and Processes
skillName: Cells as the Unit of Life

items.prompt: What is the smallest unit of a living thing that can carry out life processes?

steps: The cell is the basic unit of structure and function in living things.

items.prompt: Give one example of a unicellular organism.

steps: Unicellular organisms are made of a single cell; bacteria and amoebas are common examples.

items.prompt: Give one example of a multicellular organism.

steps: Multicellular organisms are made of many cells; animals and plants are examples.

items.prompt: According to cell theory, where do new cells come from?

steps: Cells come only from the division of cells that already exist.

items.prompt: True or false: a single bacterium is a living thing.

steps: A bacterium is made of a cell and carries out life processes, so it is living.

items.prompt: A frog is made of many cells. Is the frog unicellular or multicellular?
Why is a cell called the 'basic unit of life'?
items.answer: Because all living things are built from cells and life processes happen inside cells

steps: Cell theory names the cell as the basic unit of structure and function.

items.prompt: A student sees an organism made of one cell that feeds and reproduces. Is it alive? Explain.
items.answer: Yes, because it is made of a cell and carries out life processes

steps: Being made of a cell and carrying out life functions makes it a living thing.

items.prompt: List the three parts of cell theory.
items.answer: All living things are made of cells; the cell is the basic unit of life; cells come from existing cells

steps: These are the three statements that make up cell theory.

items.prompt: Can a living thing exist without any cells? Explain.
items.answer: No, because all living things are made of at least one cell

steps: Cell theory requires that living things be made of one or more cells.
'Uni' means one, so unicellular means one cell.
'Multi' means many, so multicellular means many cells.

items.prompt: A paramecium carries out all life functions within one cell. Is it unicellular or multicellular?

steps: One cell doing all functions is unicellular.

items.prompt: Which part of cell theory rules out cells forming from nonliving material?

steps: New cells only come from the division of existing cells.

items.prompt: Does a larger organism always have larger cells, or more cells?
items.answer: Usually more cells, not larger cells

steps: Multicellular organisms have many cells, not giant ones.
